thread:
maya: Quick sync — I'm proposing we compress the onboarding pipeline by merging the 'schema propagation' step into the prebench stage. Reason: avoids a separate heavy metadata job and reduces end-to-end latency for admit checks. Thoughts?

jon: Curious — how do you handle incremental model fingerprint changes? we rely on that separate step to generate stable identifiers.

maya: Good q. Plan is to compute a lightweight fingerprint in prebench (hash of tokenizer+shapes+top-5 param metadata) and only run the full fingerprinter in background async. The admit gates use the lightweight one for routing/compat checks.

kevin: That makes sense but I'm worried about false positives where lightweight fingerprint misses a quantization-only incompat. We then risk runtime failures.

sophia: Agree with kevin. Maybe add a targeted fast probe that runs a tiny KV/warmup scenario on a single shard to catch quant-ABI issues before admit. Cheap and quick.

maya: Exactly — fast probe + lightweight fingerprint. Fast probe runs 3 short prompts (golden inputs) on a warmup path. If it fails, we fallback to full fingerprint + bench.

jon: What about bench cost? If many models hit the fallback we'll blow budget. Can we add an acceptance policy: delta_accept_score that gates full bench only if fast-probe deviation > X?

kevin: Delta threshold is good. Suggest we calibrate X per model family (LLama2 vs meta, opt, etc.). Also annotate each model in registry with expected latency band so bench can choose shorter evaluation for tiny models.

maya: Agreed. Add per-family calibration and per-size quick-bench heuristics. We'll store calibration metadata in the model registry.

ingest-bot: NOTE: automated task created -> /tasks/INGEST-1421 "add fast-probe stage to prebench" assigned to @kevin.

kevin: I'll prototype a go/py prober that runs in 20s wall time. Implementation detail: should prober run on the same runtime image as production? if not, false mismatch possible.

maya: Prober must use the same runtime kernels and quantization flags, else it's worthless. For hosted flows we spin ephemeral instances with identical agent image. For private deployments we run a compatibility shim that mimics customer quant flags.

jon: That implies we need to standardize 'runtime-profile' metadata in the model artifact. It should include kernel hints, preferred quant modes, and tokenization quirks. Then prober + runtime can consume it.

kevin: +1. Also add a human-readable 'compatibility-notes' field for odd-ball models (eg nonstandard eos tokenization). Keeps ops from guessing.

maya: Decision proposal: Merge schema propagation into prebench, compute lightweight fingerprint, run fast-probe (same-runtime), and only dispatch full bench if fast-probe delta > family-calibrated threshold. Also attach runtime-profile and compat-notes to registry entry.

sophia: Sounds good. A couple of tradeoffs to record: 1) increases complexity in prebench orchestration 2) possible transient false negatives (we'll mitigate with async full fingerprint + nightly sweep) 3) needs extra metadata ops.

jon: I propose an opt-in for experimental models to skip fast-probe to save cycles during early research onboarding. Add a 'skip-probe' flag in intake metadata.

maya: OK opt-in flagged. Action items:
- kevin: prototype prober + add to ingest pipeline (INGEST-1421)
- jon: add runtime-profile schema + registry fields (REG-900)
- sophia: define family calibration matrix and defaults (DOCS-421)
- maya: update onboarding playbook and runbook (will PR)

kevin: I'll post a small design doc with sequence diagram. expect link tomorrow.

sophia: tl;dr: faster admits, lower avg bench cost, slightly more prebench complexity. 👍

maya: Thanks — if no major objections I'll land this as the new prebench flow by EOW.

jon: fine by me. +1

kevin: +1

ingest-bot: task INGEST-1421 status: created. "assigned": "kevin"

maya: cool, closing thread.
